title: WorkItem
description: Durable orchestration record for one deliverable issue. The controller's source of truth for orchestration; GitHub is the source of truth for facts (issue/PR/commit/merge). One WorkItem = one issue = one branch = one PR.

description.description: The issue's text outside its Acceptance section, frozen at intake like goal and acceptance (ADR-0038). WorkItems stored before this field have none.

acceptance.description: Frozen at intake. A merge is not completion until each doneWhen is checked.

paths.description: The `Paths: <glob>, <glob>` lines' globs, frozen at intake (ADR-0087): the source files this node's pass may change; the WorkOrder carries them as constraints.allowedPaths and check_pushed fails a pushed source file outside them. Null or absent means no fence. WorkItems stored before this field have none.

wallMsOverride.description: Per-item wall budget in milliseconds. Null or absent uses FACTORY_WALL_MS. Setting it never retries or resets passes.

headSha.description: The commit the controller last dispatched/observed on the branch.

reviewedSha.description: The commit the latest accepted gate verdict applies to.

gateRound.description: Mirror of pr-gatekeeper's round number. Never incremented by controller retries.

attempts.description: What was tried and what each try did, one entry per attempt. An escalation shows them.

blockedOn.description: The one thing that must be supplied before work can continue. Required while state is blocked.

waitingOn.description: The issue a ready WorkItem waits for: its issue has a 'Depends on #n' line and #n has not merged yet (ADR-0024).

passesBefore.description: Worker passes used before the last person's retry (ADR-0035). The budget counts only the passes after it.

regatedAt.description: When the last regate started a gate run (ADR-0034). A gate run that started before it does not answer that regate.

blockers.description: Fingerprinted unresolved findings, for same-problem round counting.

incident.description: The escalation this WorkItem is in, as one material identity (ADR-0081): the action that escalated it, the normalized reason and the action's own facts. A write with the same identity keeps the record and its one-answer flag; a materially changed incident is a new record and earns one fresh answer. A WorkItem escalated before this field falls back to the one-answer rule over its history.

id.description: 1 for the first record; each material change adds one.

agentAnswered.description: True once Day Desk has answered this exact incident.

causes.description: For an attempt_failed incident: the diagnostics causes of the covered attempts, deduplicated and ordered.

end.description: For a dependency_ended incident: how the dependency ended, or its status once the WorkItem resumed.

recovery.description: The autonomous recovery decision whose attempt is in flight (ADR-0081). The audit holds the decision `recovery` and its outcome `recovery_result`; this field links the two across ticks. Absent or null when none is open.

infraRetries.description: Relay losses re-queued for this WorkItem against RELAY_RETRIES_MAX (ADR-0081). A successful Result resets it.

wip.description: The kept partial work of a timed-out pass (ADR-0086, ADR-0092). New records include its kind, reviewed head and default base; old records without that provenance are retired before dispatch. Cleared when a Result completes, the PR merges, or the WorkItem ends; `moves` counts salvage pushes and stops at two.

stateVersion.description: Optimistic-concurrency version. Every durable write increments it.

providerTaskId.description: agent-relay's id for the active task.

remoteVerify.description: While state is implementing for a remote-verify repo (ADR-0045): the scratch branch that holds the patch, its commit, and when the GitHub run was waited for from. Absent or null otherwise.

owner.description: Named human owner, required while state is human_waiting.

doneWhen.description: A check read back from the produced artifact (a command, a file, a test), never from effort spent.

state.description: closed, cancelled and exhausted are terminal. merged waits for the issue to close. exhausted = budget hit, neither done nor blocked. human_waiting is NOT terminal: it is an action queue with a path back to ready or closed.

fingerprint.description: Stable hash of path + normalized problem text. Identity of 'the same problem'.
